name: Slav and Semi-Slav
when: After 1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6, or a triangle with ...d5, ...e6 and ...c6. The c8-bishop distinguishes the Slav from the Semi-Slav.
plans: Development and the d-file support a central break. After ...c5, count attackers and defenders before taking a pawn.
Balance pressure on b7 with the defence of c3 and king safety. Check the opposing bishop’s diagonal before placing a rook on it.
Central breaks and sacrifices in the Meran require calculation. Checks and material recovery take priority over general rules.

personal: Your existing 1.d4 repertoire encounters ...d5 frequently. This course separates the main Slav structures.

name: Other defences to 1.d4
description: Englund, Indian defences, Benoni, Benko and the Dutch.

name: 1…d5: Albin and queen’s pawn systems
